definition: A dependent resource is a resource that the deployment code must create or reference for the service. The parts that the provider creates automatically with the service, configured only through the attributes of the service, are excluded; a resource that the provider supplies by default when none is specified is kept. Conditional or optional resources are excluded.
quotes: copied from the live official pages on 2026-10-17; aligned with the frozen copies by src/eval/annotation.py:align (exact match, otherwise the closest sentence of the frozen page, similarity >= 0.9, logged)

resources.name: VPC
resources.quote: Amazon VPC enables you to launch AWS resources, such as Amazon EC2 instances, into a virtual network dedicated to your AWS account, known as a virtual private cloud (VPC).
resources.rationale: the instance is launched into a VPC; supplied by default when none is specified (default VPC), hence kept

resources.name: Subnet
resources.quote: When you launch an instance, you can select a subnet from the VPC.
resources.rationale: the instance is launched in a subnet of the VPC (the default subnet when none is selected), hence kept

resources.name: Security group
resources.quote: If you don't specify a security group, Amazon EC2 uses the default security group for the VPC.
resources.rationale: every instance is associated with a security group; supplied by default when none is specified (default security group), hence kept

excluded.name: Primary network interface
excluded.quote: The instance is configured with a primary network interface, which is a logical virtual network card.
excluded.reason: created automatically with the instance and configured through its attributes

excluded.name: Public IP address
excluded.quote: You can control whether the instance receives a public IP address from Amazon's pool of public IP addresses.

excluded.name: Elastic IP address
excluded.quote: If you require a persistent public IP address, you can allocate an Elastic IP address

resources.name: Virtual network
resources.quote: When you create a virtual machine (VM), you create a virtual network or use an existing one.
resources.rationale: a separate resource that the deployment code creates or references

resources.name: Subnet
resources.quote: Each NIC in a VM is connected to one subnet in one virtual network.
resources.rationale: the network interface of the VM is connected to a subnet, a separate resource of the virtual network

resources.name: Network interface
resources.quote: A virtual machine must have at least one NIC.
resources.rationale: a separate resource (not an attribute of the VM) that the deployment code creates and attaches to the VM

excluded.name: Private IP address
excluded.quote: At least one private IP address must be assigned to a VM.
excluded.reason: configured through the attributes of the network interface

excluded.name: Public IP address
excluded.quote: Assigning a public IP address to a NIC is optional.

excluded.name: Network security group
excluded.reason: optional (the portal creates one, the deployment code does not have to)

resources.name: VPC network
resources.quote: Every VM is part of a VPC network.
resources.rationale: the VM is attached to a VPC network; supplied by default when none is specified (default network), hence kept

resources.name: Subnet
resources.quote: If you omit this configuration, the `default` network and subnet are used.
resources.rationale: the VM is attached to a subnet of the VPC network (the default subnet when none is specified), hence kept

excluded.name: Virtual network interface
excluded.quote: Every compute instance in a VPC network has a default virtual network interface (vNIC).
excluded.reason: created automatically with the VM and configured through its attributes

excluded.name: Internal IPv4 address
excluded.quote: Google Cloud assigns an internal IPv4 address to the new VM from the primary IPv4 address range of the selected subnet.
